LONGGGGGGG review incoming: There's so much I want to say I don't even know where to start 😭 Maybe we'll start with the characters and actors. The casting, in my humble opinion, was NOT it. The only casting choice that felt right was Jim (and maybe Scarecrow), and everything felt wrong. They didn't feel like the characters and/or the actors weren't good at portraying them. Bruce for example? I did not see Bruce. I saw Patrick Bateman and then some guy in a mask. And that's not me trying to put the blame on Christian Bale because we all know he's an incredible actor, but there just wasn't ANYTHING to him playing Bruce/Batman that I liked or even found accurate or appealing. Yes the bases of his character are their but there's no charm to him. It doesn't feel right. And there's Alfred, who's just meh (and we all know why Michael Caine got the role 🤷🏻‍♀️). The only part I liked about the two of them was their relationship. The jokes, the care for one-another. That felt accurate. BUT THEN. We have the ATROCITY that is Liam Neeson as Ra's. What the actual flying flippity flying frick? WE STARTED OFF WITH AN ASIAN MAN PLAYING HIM (WHICH WAS MOSTLY ACCURATE), AND THEN IT TURNS OUT, THE WHITE MAN WAS HIM AFTER ALL? It's actually dreadful and so so wrong in so many ways. And then Rachel. Who's Rachel? I don't know, but she was clearly a character made simply to exist for the male lead, and will probably end up getting fridged later on. AND WHO THE HECK IS CARMINE FALCONEY? WHO'S THAT???? WHAT'S A FALCONEY??? But other than all those casting issues, I hated it. Batman feels all wrong, the whole film, while being over 2 hours long, feels like it's rushed, there's nothing gripping about it, and it feels like a film directed at men. I'm not saying it is and I'm not saying girls can't enjoy it and I'm DEFINITELY not saying Batman as a whole is for men, coming from a DC girl, but this whole film just feels like it has "male gaze" written all over it. There's no depth to anything. It's just cool car tricks and mass destruction, it doesn't feel like there's any feeling to what happens. It literally feels like- "oh, the Narrows are destroyed and lots of people most likely died. Oh well 🤷🏻‍♀️" There's no sadness to the city and it's people that are hunted and killed. That are driven to homelessness and experimented on. There's no desperation or darkness. And I think all that is why the 2022 film is so appealing to me and why it has a different audience. It's just so gripping. It's not afraid to show the horrors of Gotham. You feel the sadness and the loss of the city and it's people, including Bruce. You see how bad of a place it is, and you understand on a more personal level what Bruce tries to do. AND you actually get to see him live up to his "the world's greatest detective" nickname. You get none of that in this. He fights people, but he's only able to do that because clues fall into his lap and his told where and what he needs to do. There's no grittyness, there's not sadness. To him or the city. I also felt like a lot of it was quite cheesy </3 Like some of the jokes really didn't land well and 90% of the Batman scenes were so off putting. With the voice and the suit and the way he's written, I could barely hold myself together. And if I didn't know how popular The Dark Knight is, this film would NOT make me want to keep watching. I just feel as though this is for a certain audience of men and, because they'll probably all be same, I simply wouldn't care for the rest of the films. But my opinion is- If you like this film and hate The Batman, you like when Batman is brute force and nothing else. You like when he's a machine who doesn't have to use his brain. But he is so much more than that and so many of his films have completely missed the type of person he is supposed to be. That's why there are so many MEN that go around basically talking about a different character. Because they've only seen this films, where, in my opinion, he's partly misscharacterised. And I know this is only the first film out of the trilogy so his character might still be a bit rocky and all that, but when there is already SO much base material, literally decades worth of ground work for you to build up from, I really don't think there's any excuse. Me pareció un gran inicio para la trilogía. Lo que más me gustó fue cómo desarrolla el origen de Batman y muestra la evolución de Bruce Wayne hasta convertirse en el héroe que todos conocemos. La historia está muy bien construida y logra que entiendas perfectamente las motivaciones del personaje. Christian Bale hace un buen trabajo como Batman, aunque personalmente creo que ha tenido actuaciones mejores en otras películas. También me gustó mucho la participación de Cillian Murphy, quien aporta bastante a la historia. Mi escena favorita fue la batalla final, donde Batman se enfrenta al mal para salvar Gotham. Aunque no es mi favorita de la trilogía, sí me dejó con expectativas muy altas para la siguiente entrega y es una película que volvería a ver después de un tiempo. Algo que hace especial a esta película es la forma en que Christopher Nolan utilizó cámaras IMAX para muchas de las escenas más importantes. Esto permitió mostrar Gotham, las persecuciones y las secuencias de acción con una escala impresionante que todavía hoy se siente espectacular. Además, Nolan intentó evitar el uso excesivo de CGI, prefiriendo efectos prácticos siempre que fuera posible. Gracias a esto, muchas escenas conservan una sensación de realismo que las hace envejecer mejor que otras películas de superhéroes de la misma época. Esa combinación entre IMAX, efectos prácticos y una dirección muy cuidada es una de las razones por las que la trilogía sigue siendo tan recordada.

Since this is the first of the trilogy, here I will log some of my overall complaints about the series, before then talking specifically about this film. Overall, the series is a fairly middling and digestible watch. Superhero movies have often fallen flat for me as I get older. Most don't scratch the itch I want, and while Nolan's Batman series can grab my attention at times, I find myself bored by the end of them. Christen Bale has never really done it for me as Batman. The deep raspy voice fluctuates from silly to unbearable, and his big, weird mouth protrudes in a very unflattering way within the cowl. When he's not dawning the suit, his performance as Bruce Banner is quite good. However, in a movie about the batman, the superhero should never be overshadowed by the man. I do think that this is less a problem with Nolan and Bale and more so with the Design of Batman. To me, in live action depictions, the suit is so impractical for hand-to-hand combat that without the help of CGI, Batman looks stiff, slow, and like he's fighting with a stick up his ass. If I'm not making sense here, then imagine if Marvel committed to Iron Man's suit being completely absent of CGI. He would look like some miniature version of a Godzilla like mech and less the high-tech, lighting fast battle machine that he's supposed to be. Nolan's greatest talent is his beautiful cinematography. It's still present in the series, but most definitely more absent that I would like, however, this isn't the biggest draw back. There are more things going on and I'm sure the studio wanted the movie to be as short and concise as possible. My only gripe with the directing is the fight scenes. They are clunky and chaotic. The camera swipes between each character's bows so fast that the whole scene is one big blur of action. It almost feels as if the cameraman themselves has no idea who is going to swing next. For an action movie, the fight scenes being so poor really hampers my enjoyment. Now turning our attention to Batman Begins itself, my biggest complaint is Cillian Murphy's performance. He was just not very convincing in being this crazed insane man. He's too much of a good guy. Nolan should have hired a real demon. I also just found the Rhas al Ghul story line pretty stale. Besides that, I like Gary Oldman's performance along with Micheal Caine's. They have been bright spots along the entire series.

Chris Nolan gets a lot of flak for his sound mixing and mastering. I will say, though, that deliberately living a quasi-nomadic/homeless lifestyle in an under-developed country for no reason is a very billionaire thing to do. I absolutely loved Batman Begins, and for me, it’s the best movie in the trilogy. I know that for most people it’s The Dark Knight, and I completely understand why. But for me, Batman Begins is Nolan’s best Batman movie. Honestly, I even prefer it to The Dark Knight. The main reason is pretty simple: The Dark Knight is an incredible crime thriller with Batman and the Joker at the center of it, while Batman Begins is, above all, a movie about Batman. And I think that makes all the difference. What I love most about Begins is that it actually takes the time to show Bruce Wayne becoming Batman. He doesn’t just put on the suit and suddenly become a hero. Bruce first has to figure out what he wants Batman to represent, and why he even needs to become Batman in the first place. That’s also why I love the way the movie handles the bat itself. Bruce doesn’t choose the symbol just because it looks cool. He takes something that terrified him as a child and turns that fear into something he can control. He becomes the thing he was once afraid of. Because Batman is supposed to be frightening. He shouldn’t just be a superhero who came and beats up bad guys like TDKR . He has to be a presence, almost a legend. Something criminals think they see in the darkness. And Batman Begins understands that better than the other movies in the trilogy. Some of Batman’s first appearances are still some of my favorite moments in the movie. Nolan barely shows him at first. You see pieces of him, you hear him, you feel his presence before you really see him. He’s almost filmed like a creature hiding in the shadows. And that connects perfectly with Gotham. Gotham city feels dirty, corrupt, dangerous and almost suffocating. What I really like is that Nolan doesn’t make it feel like a giant comic-book set. He makes it feel like a real city, while still giving it that dark, almost gothic atmosphere that fits Batman perfectly. I also think Gotham reflects Bruce’s state of mind. The more he discovers about the city, the more he understands what he has to fight. And as Bruce gets closer to becoming Batman, the entire movie/photography seems to get darker with him. That’s also where I think the movie’s focus on Bruce really pays off. Ra’s al Ghul and scarecrow are important, but they never completely takes over the story. The movie is still about Bruce Wayne. It’s about his fear, his anger, his guilt, and ultimately his choice to turn all of that into something meaningful. Because Batman isn’t just the costume or the gadgets. It’s that permanent contradiction at the heart of the character: Bruce uses fear and violence to fight crime, while constantly refusing to become a murderer himself. And I think Batman Begins understands that contradiction better than the other movies. That’s ultimately why I prefer Batman Begins. The Dark Knight might be the more impressive movie overall, but Batman Begins feels more like a movie that actually understands why Batman is Batman. And for me, that matters more. Also the only real flaw I have with the movie is the fight choreography. Some of the action scenes are difficult to follow because of the way they’re shot and edited, and unfortunately, I think this becomes even more noticeable when you watch the entire trilogy specially TDKR. Looking at all three movies together, you start to realize that Nolan simply isn’t very good at choreographing hand-to-hand combat. The ideas behind the fights are often good, but the execution can feel messy and lacking in visual clarity.
